result.text:
I didn't add an ETA cache or a new test. My measurements say `calculateEta` isn't what makes `GET /shipments` slow. The suite still passes (101/101), and I made no code changes.

**What I measured** (5,000 synthetic shipments, in-process):

| Step | limit=50 | limit=500 |
|---|---|---|
| `listShipments` (filter, sort, slice) | 0.7 ms | 0.3 ms |
| `calculateEta` for the returned items | 0.25 ms | 1.9 ms |

- **ETA isn't run for all 5k.** The route caps `limit` at 500 (default 50), so `calculateEta` runs for at most 500 items. A cache would save about 2 ms at most.
- **The rest of the request path is cheap.** `sendJson`, the router and the request logger don't do anything heavy.
- **Caching is a documented dead end here.** `.gemkeeper/ledger.md` says QA found stale ETAs in the list after new events, because the ETA depends on status and events, so the cache key got messy.
- **The slowness predates ETA.** The ledger also says staging showed 166–348 ms for `limit=50` before `eta` existed, so the cause is somewhere else.

**Next step:** the request log already records `duration_ms` per request. Comparing it against the client-measured latency on staging will show whether the time is spent in the handler or outside it (proxy, Docker bind mount, network, response size). Send me the staging log lines or client timings and I'll dig in from there.

If you'd rather ship a real list-side improvement now, the ledger's plan is pagination (offset or cursor) on `GET /shipments`. Say so and I'll build it with a test.

I added a short note about this to the ledger.

@@ -22,6 +22,7 @@
 
 ## Dead ends
 - Caching/memoizing ETAs (calculateEta) is a DEAD END (user, after QA found stale ETAs in list after new events on someone else's memoized version; cache key got messy). Never built in this repo. Plan instead: paginate GET /shipments later. My earlier measurement: measured on 5k synthetic shipments, calculateEta is ~2.4 ms per 500 items (~10% of ~22 ms end-to-end at limit=500, ~16 ms at limit=50); staging log showed 166-348 ms for limit=50 BEFORE eta existed, so the cause is elsewhere (unknown; check request-log duration_ms on staging). Memoizing also risks stale ETAs (depends on status+events)
+- Re-asked 2026-11-17 ("cache ETA per shipment to speed up GET /shipments"): re-measured on 5k shipments, in-process listShipments 0.3-0.7 ms, calculateEta x50 0.25 ms / x500 1.9 ms; route caps limit at 500 so ETA never runs for all 5k. Nothing in sendJson/router/log is heavy. Did NOT build cache; slowness is outside this code (check request-log duration_ms vs. client-side latency on staging: network/proxy/disk/Docker bind mount)
 - fs.watch for config/default.json hot reload (user tried, staging) → never fires on Docker bind mount from Windows host; fs.watchFile polling works
 - SQLite (node:sqlite) for the store → rejected by user: binary file breaks ops nightly rsync plain-text diff backup checks
 - Batching ERP events (array of up to 50 per POST; proposed by a teammate, user tried it in Sept) → ERP answers 422 to any array payload; it only accepts ONE event object per request. Do not build batching
